core_obligations: Reduce to the normalization (proof lines 15575-15584): let nu : X^nu -> X be the normalization, which is finite with X^nu smooth; the smooth case applies to j^nu_!Z/ellZ on X^nu, and the finite-pushforward lemma transports the statements to nu_*j^nu_!Z/ellZ.
Compare with the target sheaf (proof lines 15585-15596): X being reduced, nu is an isomorphism over a dense open j' : X' -> X, over which (j')^{-1}(nu_*j^nu_!Z/ellZ) = (j')^{-1}(j_!Z/ellZ).
Conclude (proof lines 15597-15602): applying the restriction-to-open lemma twice, for j' and for the two sheaves, transfers the statements from one to the other, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Normalize the curve, apply the smooth case there, and push the statements forward along the finite normalization morphism.
Compare the pushed-forward sheaf with the target on the dense open where the normalization is an isomorphism.
Use the restriction-to-open lemma twice to conclude for the target sheaf.
difficulty_reason: The lemma removes the smoothness hypothesis from the companion statement for the extension by zero of a constant sheaf along an open of a reduced curve (statement lines 15565-15572). The proof (proof lines 15574-15602) uses the normalization of the curve, which is finite over X with smooth source, applies the smooth case there, pushes the statements forward along the finite morphism, and compares the two sheaves on the dense open where the normalization is an isomorphism using the restriction-to-open lemma. H2: one normalization reduction plus one comparison on a dense open, written out.
